contenders.handicapper_notes: Possesses explosive early speed (canonical style E) and lands the coveted rail draw (barrier 1) around Gosford's tight bullring circuit. Proven metropolitan juvenile form including a sharp second to Knightsbridge at Randwick. Arrives primed first-up following two dominant trial wins at Scone and Muswellbrook. Set to jump, control the fence, and exploit the short 250m straight.

Brings the strongest peak class figures into the field, having placed in the Group 3 Black Opal as a 2yo. Drops back to provincial grade following a fair fifth in a Rosehill $70k midweek maiden where she was steadied mid-race. Maps for an economical stalking trip (style P) right behind the speed from barrier 2 under Jason Collett. Genuine threat if she produces her black-type turn of foot.

High-profile debutant from the Waterhouse and Bott stable, ridden by Tim Clark. A well-bred Snitzel colt who is a full brother to Group 2 winner Best Of Bordeaux. Impressive winner of an open Randwick 1050m trial on October 23. Shows natural tactical speed (style P) and must be respected as the primary danger to the experienced market leaders.

Showed encouraging late sectionals at Canberra and Scone when closing from far back. However, his swooper running pattern (style S) faces severe headwinds around Gosford's tight turns and 250m short straight runway. Well drawn in barrier 3 to stay closer than usual, but looks best suited for exotics.

First starter by North Pacific who is a half-brother to Group-class sprinter Headwall. Trialling soundly with a close third at Rosehill, but drawing awkwardly in barrier 7 on debut puts him at risk of being trapped wide on continuous turns.

Resumes from a lengthy break with an uninspiring 0-from-12 career record. Profiles primarily as a route maiden performer, making 1200m sharp for his first-up assignment. Carries top weight of 59.0kg and is severely handicapped by the outermost barrier 9 on Gosford's tight circuit.
